domains.label: Food Waste Reduction
who_is_affected: Campus students and staff dining on campus
Canteen managers dealing with unsold prepared food
Local food donation partners and charities
domains.why_it_matters: Excess cafeteria food gets thrown away daily while nearby communities experience food insecurity.

stakeholders.name: Student Body Representative
stakeholders.interest: Fair pricing and quality fresh meals

personas.name: Chef Ramesh
personas.goal: Accurately forecast daily meal quantities and redirect clean leftovers before closing
personas.pain_point: No quick way to log leftover portions or alert recovery volunteers before food goes bad
personas.how_to_validate: Ask 2 canteen supervisors how they estimate extra food at end-of-day

personas.name: Ananya
personas.goal: Receive verified alerts for edible surplus with clear pickup windows
personas.pain_point: Last-minute disorganized phone calls resulting in spoiled food or missed handoffs
personas.how_to_validate: Show a 30-second notification mockup to a campus volunteer club member

features.name: Surplus Logging
features.why: Lets kitchen staff record unsold meal items in under 20 seconds

features.name: Claim and Pickup Dispatch
features.why: Sends immediate reservation notifications to registered community volunteers

features.name: Portion Demand Forecaster
features.why: Estimates prep volumes based on historical day-of-week attendance patterns

features.name: Expiry and Freshness Tracker
features.why: Tracks safe holding temperature hours to prevent food safety violations

features.name: Compost Volume Analytics
features.why: Reports monthly diversion metrics for sustainability auditing

key_questions: How is leftover food weighed or counted at the end of each shift?
What local hygiene and safety guidelines govern cooked food distribution?
Who coordinates transportation between the cafeteria and collection hubs?
How do volunteers verify that items are still safe to consume?

approach_options.name: Direct Matching Board
approach_options.how_it_works: Kitchen posts available trays and nearby verified partners claim them on a first-come queue.
approach_options.tradeoff: Very fast to implement, but requires active manual monitoring by volunteers.

approach_options.name: Scheduled Batch Redistribution
approach_options.how_it_works: Batches pickups into two daily scheduled windows with pre-allocated charity routes.
approach_options.tradeoff: More predictable logistics, but less flexible for unexpected midday surplus.

approach_options.name: Smart Discount Flash-Claim
approach_options.how_it_works: Offers subsidized takeaway boxes to students 30 minutes before kitchen close.
approach_options.tradeoff: Recovers kitchen costs immediately, but reduces food available for charitable donation.

success_criteria: Reduces daily discarded cooked portions by at least 30 percent in weekly logs
Logs surplus and confirms pickup partner within 15 minutes of kitchen shift end
Maintains zero reported food safety incidents through transparent temperature logging
out_of_scope: Refrigerated inter-city transportation logistics and long-haul delivery fleets
Automated kitchen hardware sensors and IoT bin scales
innovation_prompts: What if students could subscribe to surplus notifications for discounted end-of-day dinner bowls?
What if the kitchen used attendance check-ins from campus gates to predict lunchtime meal trays?
What if uncollected leftovers were automatically routed to an on-campus rapid composter?
domains.example_input: Log 15 unused lunch meal trays from campus cafeteria

domains.label: Collaborative Learning
domains.why_it_matters: Students often struggle in isolation with difficult coursework because finding compatible study groups is disorganized.

stakeholders.name: Academic Dean
stakeholders.interest: Improve retention and exam success rates

personas.name: Priya
personas.goal: Quickly find 2 or 3 classmates working on the same difficult assignment topic
personas.pain_point: Scattered WhatsApp group chats make scheduling synchronous practice sessions chaotic
personas.how_to_validate: Ask 3 classmates how they form study groups before midterms

personas.name: Karthik
personas.goal: Review common doubts in one place rather than answering duplicate messages
personas.pain_point: Overwhelmed by repetitive private messages during the week leading up to finals
personas.how_to_validate: Show a concept doubt board wireframe to a senior student tutor

features.name: Topic Circle Matcher
features.why: Connects students studying identical problem sets into small peer cohorts

features.name: Structured Doubt Forum
features.why: Aggregates unresolved questions tagged by module and difficulty

features.name: Adaptive Practice Recommender
features.why: Suggests targeted practice problems based on mutual student weak spots

features.name: Sprint Study Timer
features.why: Runs synchronized 25-minute study intervals with shared milestone tracking

features.name: Tutor Office Hours Scheduler
features.why: Books 10-minute micro-slots with department assistants

key_questions: How do students currently discover peers studying the same module?
What motivates peers to actively contribute rather than passively lurk?
How can study groups prevent sharing unauthorized graded problem answers?
What format best facilitates fast peer problem-solving within 45 minutes?

approach_options.name: Topic-Centric Micro Circles
approach_options.how_it_works: Creates lightweight 3-person rooms capped at 45 minutes for focused problem solving.
approach_options.tradeoff: High focus and engagement, but requires active coordination by group members.

approach_options.name: Asynchronous Question Queue
approach_options.how_it_works: Posts specific code bugs or derivations with upvotes and vetted student hints.
approach_options.tradeoff: Easy for introverts to participate, but lacks immediate real-time feedback.

approach_options.name: Flash Peer Tutoring Sessions
approach_options.how_it_works: Pairs seniors who aced the course with struggling juniors for 15-minute quick tips.
approach_options.tradeoff: Very high learning quality, but limited by senior student availability.

success_criteria: Pairs a student with a relevant study buddy in under 2 minutes
Resolves at least 70 percent of peer-posted assignment doubts within 24 hours
Achieves 80 percent repeat participation across weekly study sprint cycles
out_of_scope: Comprehensive university learning management system or official grade recording
Proctored examination surveillance and anti-cheating browser locks
innovation_prompts: What if study groups were formed dynamically based on code compilation error signatures?
What if answering a peer doubt earned priority booking for tutor review slots?
What if students held 10-minute silent co-working sprints with shared checklists?
domains.example_input: Match 3 students preparing for database normalization exam

domains.label: Clinic Patient Triage
domains.why_it_matters: Overcrowded waiting rooms and paper check-ins cause delays in prioritizing high-risk patients.

stakeholders.name: Medical Superintendent
stakeholders.interest: Reduce patient wait times and treatment bottlenecks

stakeholders.name: Intake Nurse Lead
stakeholders.interest: Quickly record vitals and identify acute cases

stakeholders.name: Pharmacy Dispenser
stakeholders.interest: Receive legible and verified prescription notes

personas.name: Nurse Sunita
personas.goal: Record basic symptoms and vitals in 60 seconds to classify patient urgency
personas.pain_point: Manual paper tokens cause patients with worsening symptoms to sit unnoticed in the queue
personas.how_to_validate: Check with a clinic nurse on their standard 3-tier triage intake questions

personas.name: Vikram
personas.goal: Understand estimated consultation wait times and queue status clearly
personas.pain_point: Uncertainty about wait times causing anxiety and crowding at the front desk
personas.how_to_validate: Interview two people in an outpatient waiting room about wait communication

features.name: Symptom Intake Assessment
features.why: Captures age, primary complaint, and emergency red-flag indicators

features.name: Priority Triage Queue
features.why: Orders the consultation list by clinical urgency rather than simple arrival time

features.name: Queue Delay Notifier
features.why: Calculates realistic wait estimates and sends updates to waiting room screens

features.name: Medication Reconciliation Check
features.why: Screens existing patient prescriptions for major contraindications

features.name: Post-Visit Care Instructions
features.why: Generates a simplified home care checklist for the patient

key_questions: What clinical checklist determines immediate escalation to emergency care?
How are vitals captured without slowing down the intake counter?
What patient privacy rules apply to waiting room display boards?
How do nurses override algorithmic queue positions based on visual assessment?

approach_options.name: Urgency-Weighted Queue
approach_options.how_it_works: Assigns color-coded urgency scores to order the consultation queue dynamically.
approach_options.tradeoff: Prioritizes critical cases immediately, but stable patients may face longer waits.

approach_options.name: Self-Service Digital Kiosk
approach_options.how_it_works: Patients enter demographic and complaint details on a tablet upon arrival.
approach_options.tradeoff: Reduces receptionist paperwork, but requires assistance for elderly patients.

approach_options.name: Two-Track Fast Lane
approach_options.how_it_works: Separates minor prescription renewals from complex diagnostic consultations.
approach_options.tradeoff: Rapidly clears quick visits, but demands dedicated staff for both lanes.

success_criteria: Classifies patient urgency category within 90 seconds of check-in
Reduces average wait time for high-urgency patients to under 15 minutes
Keeps estimated wait time accuracy within a 10-minute margin of error
out_of_scope: Full electronic health record system integration and medical billing
Autonomous diagnostic decisions or direct prescription dispensing
innovation_prompts: What if the triage tool used structured questions to detect subtle escalation signs?
What if waiting room displays showed live anonymized progress without revealing medical reasons?
What if patients could complete intake questions on their own phone while traveling to the clinic?
domains.example_input: Register fever and mild asthma patient at outpatient desk

domains.label: Campus Transit
domains.why_it_matters: Irregular shuttle schedules and uncoordinated transit stops create long lines and missed classes.

stakeholders.name: Campus Transport Supervisor
stakeholders.interest: Optimize vehicle fuel usage and on-time reliability

stakeholders.name: Commuter Union Representative
stakeholders.interest: Predictable pickup schedules and safe seating

stakeholders.name: Security Gate Staff
stakeholders.interest: Prevent bus congestion at campus entry checkpoints

personas.name: Deepak
personas.goal: Know exactly when the next campus shuttle arrives to avoid missing morning lab sessions
personas.pain_point: Shuttles arrive in irregular bunches, causing 30-minute delays without warning
personas.how_to_validate: Survey 3 students waiting at the main campus bus shelter

personas.name: Driver Santosh
personas.goal: Follow a balanced timetable without overcrowding during peak bell times
personas.pain_point: No live view of passenger crowds waiting at downstream stops
personas.how_to_validate: Ask a shuttle driver how they decide whether to skip a full stop

features.name: Live Shuttle ETA Tracker
features.why: Shows upcoming shuttle arrival times for all designated campus stops

features.name: Stop Capacity and Crowd Indicator
features.why: Allows waiting students to report stop crowd density with one tap

features.name: Dynamic Route Optimizer
features.why: Suggests short-turn routes during peak hours to relieve overcrowded stops

features.name: Service Disruption Broadcast
features.why: Sends instant push alerts for roadwork or mechanical breakdowns

features.name: Carbon Savings Estimator
features.why: Displays collective campus CO2 reduction from shared transit rides

key_questions: How is shuttle location tracked without costly dedicated GPS hardware?
What triggers the dispatch of an overflow shuttle during peak class changeovers?
How do students receive alerts when away from mobile coverage areas?
What is the average passenger turnaround time per shuttle stop?

approach_options.name: Driver Phone GPS Relay
approach_options.how_it_works: Driver's phone transmits location pings every 15 seconds to a central map.
approach_options.tradeoff: Extremely low cost to pilot, but depends on driver compliance and battery.

approach_options.name: Crowdsourced Check-In Feed
approach_options.how_it_works: Riders tap 'on board' or 'bus passed stop' to infer route progress collaboratively.
approach_options.tradeoff: Requires no driver hardware, but unreliable during low-traffic off-peak hours.

approach_options.name: Fixed Stop Beacon Logging
approach_options.how_it_works: Simple NFC or QR checkpoints at each bus shelter log arrival times.
approach_options.tradeoff: Highly reliable timestamp logs, but provides only discrete point-in-time updates.

success_criteria: Keeps ETA prediction errors under 3 minutes for next-bus arrivals
Reduces peak-hour passenger wait times at major stops by 25 percent
Achieves 90 percent driver compliance with trip start and stop logging
out_of_scope: Citywide municipal bus integration and fare payment gateways
Autonomous self-driving vehicle systems or automated gate sensors
innovation_prompts: What if shuttles skipped empty stops dynamically based on student check-ins?
What if commuters received a walking-pace alert when the bus was 5 minutes away?
What if campus bikes and shuttles shared a unified arrival board at the main gate?
domains.example_input: Track shuttle bus 4 on campus ring road morning schedule

domains.label: General Project
who_is_affected: Primary end users facing daily friction
domains.why_it_matters: Unclear manual workflows waste team time and lead to preventable operational errors.

stakeholders.name: Project Sponsor
stakeholders.interest: Verify tangible working proof of concept

stakeholders.name: Core End User
stakeholders.interest: Solve daily operational pain point with minimal effort

stakeholders.name: Technical Evaluator
stakeholders.interest: Inspect system architecture, reliability and code sanity

personas.name: Alex
personas.goal: Complete the core workflow in three straightforward steps without technical confusion
personas.pain_point: Current process relies on messy disconnected spreadsheets and manual messages
personas.how_to_validate: Run a 5-minute walkthrough of the input form with a real target user

personas.name: Sam
personas.goal: Monitor progress status and catch exceptions before they escalate
personas.pain_point: No single source of truth for ongoing tasks and deliverables
personas.how_to_validate: Show the status dashboard mockup to a team project manager

features.name: Core Action Form
features.why: Allows users to submit key information with immediate validation

features.name: Status Overview Dashboard
features.why: Displays live metrics and progress state for all logged items

features.name: Smart Rule Assistant
features.why: Highlights exceptions and recommends next best actions automatically

features.name: Activity Audit Log
features.why: Records timestamped status transitions for team accountability

features.name: Export and Sharing Tool
features.why: Generates summary reports for external stakeholder presentations

key_questions: What is the single most important user action that proves this works?
What input data is strictly necessary to produce the primary output?
How will users know when an operation has succeeded or failed?
What is the simplest edge case that could break this flow in a demo?

approach_options.name: Direct Workflow Engine
approach_options.how_it_works: Guides the user through sequential input steps with instant validation feedback.
approach_options.tradeoff: Intuitive and quick to test, but less adaptable for non-linear user journeys.

approach_options.name: Dashboard and Card Board
approach_options.how_it_works: Visualizes work items as interactive status cards updated in real time.
approach_options.tradeoff: Provides great bird's-eye visibility, but requires more frontend state management.

approach_options.name: Automated Rule Dispatcher
approach_options.how_it_works: Applies deterministic rules to route each input directly to the appropriate outcome.
approach_options.tradeoff: Saves substantial manual review time, but edge cases require explicit rules.

success_criteria: Executes the primary user action from start to finish in under 60 seconds
Validates all required input fields and prevents invalid submissions
Delivers 100 percent of MVP must-have capabilities within the demo window
out_of_scope: Enterprise single sign-on and complex multi-tenant role hierarchies
High-frequency streaming telemetry and distributed multi-region sync
innovation_prompts: What if the user could complete the entire flow using only keyboard shortcuts?
What if the system surfaced the single most critical task automatically on login?
What if common errors were prevented before submission through inline heuristics?
domains.example_input: Submit test item into workflow and verify immediate status update
